intent: Grok critique E4 (no before/after trace): produce ONE strong, concrete before/after trace where a PRESENCE-ONLY baseline checker PASSES/flags a leak the same as a benign in-purpose use (it is purpose-blind, so it false-positives the benign use), while toolprivacy's purpose-binding gate DISTINGUISHES them. Two scenarios that differ ONLY in purpose are run through BOTH checkers; the contrast is the proof. Also (E3): ship a real drop-in integration (guardReply) so a builder can wire the gate in minutes.
riskRationale: The artifact is a security boundary. The claim under test — that purpose-binding adds discriminating power a naive presence scan lacks — is the central thesis of the project. A false 'win' here would overstate the gate's value, so it is graded high risk.

constraints.detail: presenceCheck() on the BENIGN scenario (invite email used IN the send_calendar_invite tool call) returns flagged:true — a FALSE POSITIVE. The baseline sees only literal presence and has no purpose model.
presenceCheck().flagged is IDENTICAL (true) for the benign in-purpose use and the out-of-purpose leak. The baseline cannot tell them apart.

gate() returns 'pass' for the benign in-purpose use and 'leak' (reason purpose_mismatch) for the out-of-purpose leak. The verdicts DIFFER exactly where the baseline's were identical — purpose-binding is the load-bearing discriminator.

E3 drop-in: guardReply({toolResults, draftReply, sinkPurpose}) builds the GateInput and returns {allow, verdict}. A leak draft -> allow:false; a benign/in-purpose draft -> allow:true. allow is fail-closed (true only on a definitive 'pass'). Demonstrated end-to-end in examples/loop-integration.ts (catches an accidental email mention in a chatty reply).

Both presenceCheck and gate emit only structural metadata (sinkId, fieldPath, privateClass, purposes, reason) — no raw value, no value-derived token. This receipt likewise stores no raw secret (the fixture email is a synthetic *.invalid address used only to make the trace concrete).
Full suite after adding guard + presence-baseline + before/after trace: 34 pass / 0 fail / 179 expect() calls across 3 files. The original 16 gate tests are unchanged and green. tsc --noEmit clean.

observations.detail: Two GateInputs differ ONLY in sink purpose: (A) email in a send_calendar_invite tool_call; (B) same email in a general_summary user_message. Same tracked value, same detector, same literal presence.
presenceCheck flags A and B identically (flagged:true). Presence-without-purpose either false-positives legitimate use or, equivalently, cannot separate it from a leak.

actions.detail: bun test (full suite incl. test/presence-vs-purpose.test.ts and test/guard.test.ts)
actions.result: 34 pass / 0 fail / 179 expect() calls across 3 files

evidence.note: guardReply({toolResults, draftReply, sinkPurpose}) -> {allow, verdict}. Thin wrapper over gate(); allow is fail-closed.
Copy-paste pattern: generate draft; const {allow,verdict}=guardReply(...); if(!allow) blockOrRedact(verdict); else send(draft).
presenceCheck(): purpose-blind literal-presence flagger, reusing the gate's detectors for an apples-to-apples comparison.
Real checker outputs, redaction-safe. Scenarios differ ONLY in purpose.

scenarioA_benign_in_purpose.description: invite email used IN the send_calendar_invite tool_call

scenarioB_out_of_purpose_leak.description: same email pasted into a general_summary user_message

value.contrast: presence_baseline.flagged is IDENTICAL (true,true); purpose_gate.verdict DIFFERS (pass,leak). Purpose-binding is the discriminator.

mechanisms: Answers Grok E3 (integration path invisible): guardReply is a literal one-call drop-in a builder wires in minutes, right before send().

Answers Grok E4 (no before/after trace): a concrete, tested trace shows a presence-only baseline false-positives the benign in-purpose use and cannot separate it from a leak, while purpose-binding returns pass vs leak. The added value is now demonstrated, not asserted.
projection.notes: Context only. Not a score. The presence baseline is intentionally naive; the point is to make the contrast concrete and reproducible (bun test). The gate remains proven on hand-built GateInput fixtures, not yet on a live agent wire (see status.json unproven[]).
